reference: Bash metadata and documented escdelay default, inclusive range, independent fixed state-transition and environment-precedence contracts. No matching GNU CLI exists.
coverage: Bash reports escdelay as a loadable builtin.
The help metadata advertises the documented get/set forms, 50 ms default, and inclusive 0..5000 ms range.
The help metadata documents per-screen and global lookup precedence.
Deferred operation scope: global and per-screen state, environment overrides, argument validation, and actual decoder timing integration.
Operation contracts: global/default state, inclusive bounds, per-screen/environment precedence, rejected arguments, updates at the documented 16-screen capacity.
exclusions: Only actual ESC/CSI timing integration requires a disposable PTY/input decoder and controllable clock; state operations use no terminal.

cases.purpose: Check Bash type metadata identifies the registered escdelay command as a builtin.
Check the help metadata publishes the get/set syntax, default, and supported inclusive millisecond range.
cases.script:
doc=$(help escdelay)
[[ $doc == *"escdelay set [--screen NAME] MS"* ]]
[[ $doc == *"escdelay get [--screen NAME]"* ]]
[[ $doc == *"escdelay --help | --version"* ]]
[[ $doc == *"Default: 50 ms"* ]]
[[ $doc == *"Bounds:  0..5000 ms inclusive"* ]]
printf 'usage-range\n'

cases.purpose: Check help documents the per-screen environment/state and global environment/state lookup order.
cases.script:
doc=$(help escdelay)
[[ $doc == *"Precedence (highest wins):"* ]]
[[ $doc == *"BASHESCDELAY_SCREEN_<NAME> env (per-screen GET only)"* ]]
[[ $doc == *"builtin per-screen state"* ]]
[[ $doc == *"BASHESCDELAY env"* ]]
[[ $doc == *"builtin global state"* ]]
[[ $doc == *"Default: 50"* ]]
printf 'precedence\n'

cases.purpose: Specify future integration coverage that demonstrates the configured grace interval changes bare-ESC versus CSI decoding.
cases.reason: Remaining obligations: r1: Configured state and the resulting decoder mismatch are observed on both builds. The original controlled-clock requirement is under review; current tests use timed pipes and tolerant real-time windows.

cases.purpose: Default and successive global updates cover both inclusive bounds and persistence in the calling shell.
cases.script:
unset BASHESCDELAY
escdelay get
escdelay set 0
escdelay get
escdelay set 5000
escdelay get
escdelay set 73
escdelay get

cases.purpose: Per-screen env, per-screen state, global env, global state and invalid-env fallthrough follow the published precedence.
cases.script:
unset BASHESCDELAY BASHESCDELAY_SCREEN_main
escdelay set 80
escdelay get --screen main
export BASHESCDELAY=90
escdelay get --screen main
escdelay set --screen main 120
escdelay get --screen main
export BASHESCDELAY_SCREEN_main=140
escdelay get --screen main
escdelay get
export BASHESCDELAY_SCREEN_main=invalid
escdelay get --screen main
unset BASHESCDELAY_SCREEN_main
export BASHESCDELAY=5001
escdelay get
escdelay get --screen other

cases.purpose: Rejected ordinary out-of-range and malformed values return usage status and preserve existing state.
cases.script:
escdelay set 42
for value in -1 5001 nope 1.5 ''; do
 if escdelay set "$value"; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
 printf '%s\n' "$rc"
 [[ $rc == 2 ]]
done
escdelay get

cases.purpose: Missing or extra arguments and invalid screen names reject with diagnostics.
cases.script:
for args in 'set' 'get extra' 'get --screen' 'set --screen bad-name 4' 'get --screen bad/name' 'set 1 extra' 'unknown'; do
 read -r -a words <<< "$args"
 if escdelay "${words[@]}"; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
 printf '%s\n' "$rc"
 [[ $rc == 2 ]]
done

cases.purpose: Sixteen documented screen slots accept updates and reject a seventeenth distinct screen without changing existing values.
cases.script:
for ((i=0;i<16;i++)); do escdelay set --screen "screen_$i" "$i"; done
escdelay set --screen screen_0 88
escdelay get --screen screen_0
if escdelay set --screen overflow 2; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
printf '%s\n' "$rc"
[[ $rc == 1 ]]
escdelay get --screen screen_15
